# Clearbyte

> A tool for creating custom cloud computing lab activities. Instructors author a lab as small ordered steps; students complete it in a real AWS account launched from the course LMS; work is graded automatically against what was built in that account.

Clearbyte was built by a cloud computing instructor who wanted lab activities that could be shaped around what students were actually struggling with, rather than using a prebuilt catalog as provided. It is now shared with other colleges and universities.

Key facts:

- Instructors write and revise the labs themselves, including mid-semester.
- Labs are broken into small steps, so it is visible which step a class stalls on.
- Each student gets a real AWS account, provisioned at launch and destroyed when the lab ends.
- Labs launch from the course LMS over LTI 1.3; used with Canvas today.
- Grading inspects what was built in the AWS account and returns a score to the gradebook.
- Runs exclusively on AWS. Every part of the platform is built on AWS services.
- Deliberately designed around on-demand AWS services (Lambda, Step Functions, DynamoDB on-demand billing) so it is inexpensive to run. No servers, load balancers or databases idle between labs, and cost tracks actual use.
- It is a lab authoring and delivery tool, not a drop-in curriculum.
- Access is arranged directly by contacting Clearbyte, not by self-signup.
